callees_evidence.identity: OBSERVED in full, 43 instructions. It is a guarded state setter on the same receiver: it writes +0x84, truncates the two wchar buffers at +0x14c and +0x15c, and only performs an App::IAppSystem::Init(0x13eb844) transition when the new value is 3.

semantic_contract: 0x00c485b0 is a zero-argument mode setter. It forwards its ECX receiver and the literal 2 to 0x00c47cc0 and tail-returns, so the entire observable effect of 0x00c485b0 is the effect of that one call. For the constant 2 that effect is fully determined and fully reachable: if the receiver's dword at +0x84 already equals 2 the call does nothing at all, making the setter idempotent; otherwise +0x84 is set to 2, the wchar-terminated buffer whose base is at +0x14c is truncated to an empty string and its cursor at +0x150 is rewound to that base, and the same truncation-and-rewind is applied to the second buffer at +0x15c/+0x160. 0x00c47cc0 then tests the new value against 3 and returns, because 2 is not 3; the App::IAppSystem::Init state-switch block that would follow is statically unreachable from 0x00c485b0. The function therefore has no return value, no error path and no observable read outside the receiver. The +0x15c/+0x160 pair it clears is the same pair that 0x00c70150 treats as a pointer-vector, which is what ties the two functions to one receiver class.
classification_rationale: All eight bytes of the body, the tail-call structure, the ABI, the callee's full 43-instruction body, every field offset, every immediate and every branch polarity are read directly from the disassembly, and the reachability of the state-switch block is proved from the constant rather than assumed. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld for one named bound: the class of the receiver is not established. SporeApp.exe has no MSVC RTTI, no vtable was located for the receiver, neither 0x00c485b0 nor 0x00c47cc0 appears in any .rdata or .data slot, and no ModAPI header declares a class with a dword at +0x84, two adjacent wchar cursors at +0x14c/+0x150 and a pointer pair at +0x15c/+0x160 followed by a kind field at +0x194. The bound is the owning type; the behaviour carries no residual uncertainty. A second, smaller bound is recorded for completeness: the concrete target of the virtual call at 0x00c47d62 is unresolved, but that call is unreachable.
semantic_findings: 0x00c485b0 is a pure forwarder: PUSH 2, CALL 0x00c47cc0, RET. There is no other instruction and no other effect.
Because 0x00c47cc0 ends in RET 4, the sequence is a tail call and the original caller resumes from the callee's epilogue; no value is produced or consumed.
The reachable effect of the constant 2 is: set the receiver's +0x84 to 2 and clear two wchar-terminated buffers, with an idempotence guard on the mode field.

The App::IAppSystem::Init(0x13eb844) state switch inside 0x00c47cc0 is dead for mode 2, proved by 0x00c47d17/0x00c47d1e rather than assumed. The same callee reaches it for mode 3, so the setter family is a state machine whose interesting state is 3, not 2.

The two buffers truncated here are addressed by the same +0x15c/+0x160 offsets that 0x00c70150 subtracts to get an element count, so the receiver carries both a text buffer and an indexable list, and switching the mode invalidates both.
0x00c485b0 and 0x00c47cc0 are in no vtable, so this is a free helper on a concrete class rather than an interface method, and no SDK name can be attached to it.
unresolved_questions: The binary carries no MSVC RTTI, so no class identity can be read from typeinfo; class claims in this record rest only on observed vtable data and SDK header text.
No original-process trace exists for any function in this batch. Every statement here is static.
What class owns 0x00c485b0? The offset signature (+0x84 mode, +0x14c/+0x150 and +0x15c/+0x160 wchar cursors, +0x194 kind) matches no ModAPI declaration, and no vtable for the receiver was located.

What is the value 3 that unlocks the App::IAppSystem::Init(0x13eb844) transition, and which caller performs it? Only 0x00c485b0 (value 2) and 0x00c47d80 (unconditional variant) were located in this session; a caller of 0x00c47cc0 with 3 was not found.

Is 0x00c47d80 the same operation without the mode guard? Its body clears both buffers and then always runs the Init transition, with no comparison against the incoming value, which suggests the pair is 'transition unconditionally' versus 'transition if the mode actually changes'.
Why do the two buffers get truncated on every mode change? The evidence shows that it happens; it does not show whether the old contents are meant to be discarded or re-derived.
Fifteen of the sixteen observed call sites were not disassembled, so the context in which mode 2 is selected is unverified.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has been captured for 0x00c485b0, so the claim that the +0x84 write is the only persistent effect is static-only.
A runtime differential test must confirm that 0x00c47cc0's RET 4 still matches in the shipping build, since the whole tail-call reading depends on it.
The value stored at +0x84 before and after each of the 16 call sites must be observed to confirm the idempotence guard is exercised rather than always false.
